newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital market closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital market closing report.

text.p: The French 10-year bond future settled weaker but off its lows in thin range-bound trade with the market waiting for U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress later this week.
Analysts said the market was on standby ahead of Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony on Wednesday and Thursday.
"People are just focusing on that and waiting," said one trader. The lack of other market-moving news meant there was little impetus to buy or to sell, he added.
A weaker tone to U.S. Treasuries also undermined the market.
The March bond future contract retraced after breaking through support at 132.06 to touch a low of 132.04. It finished down 14 basis points at 132.12.
One analyst said he believed 132.06 would continue to hold as a support point thanks to buying by portfolio managers.
Analysts said that the bond future's consolidation over the last few trading days did not put into question its underlying bullish trend.
"But the markets cannot get too excited because they need to have some ideas about the FOMC meeting on March 25. That's why Greenspan's testimony to Congress is so important," one said.
The franc held steady at 3.3751/56 per mark against 3.3756/60 on Friday.

Analysts said they did not expect a reduction in the Bank of France's intervention rate after this Thursday's monetary policy council meeting but added that if the franc continued to appreciate, there might be a cut.
